subject: Re: load_all() error with 64bit R: %1 is not a valid Win32 application.

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: load_all() error with 64bit R: %1 is not a valid Win32 application.
parts:
Is there a reason that you're using old style Rcpp, instead of new
style Rcpp with attributes?

Hadley

On Wed, Mar 19, 2014 at 8:17 AM, Kurt Z <yzha...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi All,
>
> I am a new devtools user and I am practicing with a very small project on a
> 64bit Windows 7 PC. I wrote only two files:
>
> package_path/R/r-fun.R
> package_path/src/c-fun.cpp
>
> When I tried to load_all() my package using 32bit R, it works all fine.
> However, if I try to load_all() the package using 64bit R, it gave me an
> error message saying:
>
> Error in inDL(x, as.logical(local), as.logical(now), ...) :
> unable to load shared object 'path-to-package/src/myPackage.dll':
> LoadLibrary failure: %1 is not a valid Win32 application.
>
> Any idea why is this?
>
> Best Regards
> Yue Z
>
> ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
> ## Sourcecode: package_path/src/c-fun.cpp
>
> #include <Rcpp.h>
>
> using namespace Rcpp;
>
> RcppExport SEXP test(SEXP x_) {
> BEGIN_RCPP;
>
> List x(x_);
> x["addedField"] = NumericVector::create(1.0, 2.0, 3.0);
>
> return x;
>
> END_RCPP;
> }
>
> ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
> ## Soucecde: package_path/R/r-fun.R
> rtest <- function(x) {
> x <- as.list(x)
> .Call("test", x, PACKAGE="yzQuantLib")
> }
>
